I could not get a complete list of failing files from this run. The output was truncated in the middle, and the final pass/fail summary is missing, so I have not rerun it.

**Confirmed failing files** (failures visible in the output):
- `tests/test_arguments.py` (F marks in the progress line)
- `tests/test_basic.py` (F marks)
- `tests/test_commands.py` (F marks)
- `tests/test_context.py` (F marks)
- `tests/test_options.py` (F marks)
- `tests/test_parser.py` (`FFFFF`, five failures)
- `tests/test_utils/test_echo_via_pager.py` (traceback: `test_echo_via_pager[test0- less ]`, `assert '' == 'just text\n'`)

**Unknown:** Files in the truncated section, between `tests/test_utils/test__expand_args.py` and the end of the progress output, may also have failures. I can't see their progress lines.

**Other things to know about this run:**
- Pytest reported `collected 33653 items / 31000 deselected / 2653 selected`. So only 2,653 tests ran, not the whole suite. The deselection comes from configuration, probably `pyproject.toml`, but I did not check why.
- Some failures show `pager == ''` where the expected output is `just text\n`. The `echo_via_pager` tests use a real pager subprocess, so this could be an environment issue, but I have not investigated.

I did not modify any repo files. Pytest may have written its usual `.pytest_cache` directory.

To get the full list, I can rerun with output written to a file outside the repo, for example `/tmp/pytest-full.log`, and then grep the `FAILED` lines. That needs your go-ahead, since you asked for a single run.
